HON. JAYVEE TYRON L. UY, MPA Vice Governor, Province of Davao de Oro SP Office, Legislative Bldg., Provincial Capitol Cabidianan, Nabunturan, Davao de Oro Dear Vice Governor Uy: This has reference to your letter dated January IO, 2024, requesting this Department's opinion regarding the 2024 Annual Investment Program (AIP), which motion for its approval and adoption was denied by a majority vote of the members of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan (SP). As represented, the CY 2024 AIP was disapproved by the sanggunian by a vote of 8-5 (negative and affirmative votes, respectively), but later vetoed by the Governor. Hence, the issue proffered is whether the Provincial Governor can veto a resolution disapproving the CY 2024 AIP. Culled from your letter are the following pertinent factual antecedents: On October 11, 2023, the provincial government of Davao de Oro (PDC) Resolution No. 39, Series of 2023, entitled : A Resolution Adopting the Additional Programs, Projects and Activities (PPAs) and Adjustments of PPA Funding Requirements and Expense Classification, to the Previously Adopted and Endorsed CY 2024 Annual Investment Program (CY 2024 AIP), and Endorsing a New Copy of the CY 2024 AIP Incorporating the Additional PPAs and Adjustment of PPA Funding Requirements and Expense Classification with the Total Amount of Seven Billion Seven Hundred Fifty One Million Six Hundred Forty Nine Thousand Nine Hundred Eighty Two Pesos and 73/100 (P7, 751, 649,982.730 for Programs, Projects and Activities Under the General Fund, and Eight Billion One Hundred Ninety-Two Million Thirty-Seven Thousand Pesos (P8, 192, 037, 000.00) for Funding from other Sources, Totaling to Fifteen Billion Nine Hundred Forty- Three Million Six Hundred Eighty-Six Thousand Nine Hundred Eighty-Two Pesos and 73/100 was endorsed to the SP and was discussed during the 3rd Special Session. On October 25, 2023, the Office of the Secretary to the Sanggunian received a letter from Governor Dorothy P. Montejo-Gonzaga endorsing for perusal and immediate action of the veto to sp Resolution Nos. 0972-20231, 0973-20232, 1 RESOLUTION NO. 0972-2023, ENTITLED "RECOMMENDING TO AMEND, THE ENDORSED AMENDMENTS OF THE cy 2024 AIP PARTICULARLY LOGISTICAL SUPPORT TO FORCE MULTIPLIERS - BARANGAY PEACE BUILDING WORKERS UNDER THE PROVINCIAL PEACE AND ORDER AND PUBLIC SAFETY PROGRAM, TO INCLUDE THE BARANGAY HEALTH WORKERS PROGRAM. 2 RESOLUTION NO 0972-2023. ENTITLED: "THE ENDORSED AMENDMENT OF THE cy 2024 AIP WERE EXHAUSTIVELY DISCUSSED IN THE PLENARY, AFTER WHICH. A MOTION WAS RAISED FOR THE PASSAGE OF A RESOLUTION RECOMMENDING TO AMEND LOGISTICAL SUPPORT TO FORCE MULTIPLIERS - TRIBAL CHIEFTAINS UNDER PROVINCIAL PEACE AND ORDER AND PUBLIC SAFETY PROGRAM, TO INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING: INDIGENOUS POLITICAL STRUCTURE: MTC. IPO, ADMO, IP WOMEN, IP YOUTH, AND BARANGAY TRIBAL CHIEFTAIN." "Matino, Mahusay, at Maaasahan" Trunkline: (02) 8876-3454

0974-20233 and 0975-20234. During its 74th Regular Session dated December 5, 2023, the said CY 2024 AIP was discussed under the Unassigned Business of the Agenda, which was duly moved for its adoption but was objected to; hence, a nominal vote was called for the purpose, which resulted in five (5) affirmative and eight (8) negative votes. Accordingly, the sanggunian passed Resolution No. 1079-2023, entitled "A Resolution Informing the Honorable Governor, Dorothy P. Montejo-Gonzaga, of the Action of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan Denying the Motion for Approval of the CY 2024 Annual Investment Program (AIP) of Davao de Oro Province". On December 20, 2023, the Office of the Secretary to the Sanggunian received a letter from the Governor endorsing for information, perusal, and immediate action of the Veto for SP Resolution No. 1079-2023. It is intimated that the sangguaniang members have differing views regarding the power of the LCE to veto the SP Resolution disapproving the CY AIP. Hence, the subject issue. At the outset, it may be well to touch on the signification of veto. Veto is defined as the refusal of assent by the executive officer whose assent is necessary to perfect a law that has been passed by the legislative body and the message that is usually sent to such a body by the executive, stating such refusal and the reasons therefor (Black's Law Dictionary, 5th Ed. , 1983). In the context of local governments, veto refers to the power of the local chief executive (LCE)—i.e., governors, mayors, and punong barangays—to reject certain ordinances or resolutions passed by the sanggunian. Fundamentally, it is designed to serve as a mechanism for LCE to obviate the enactment of an ordinance or the passage of a resolution that he deems infirmed or not in the best interest of the general public or their constituents. Having laid down the foregoing, attention is now respectfully invited to the pertinent provisions of the Local Government Code of 1991 (Republic Act No. 7160, hereinafter referred to as the Code), thus: Section 54 of the Code reads: "Section 54. Approval of Ordinances. - (a) Every ordinance enacted by the sangguniang panlalawigan, sangguniang panlungsod, or sangguniang bayan shall be presented to the provincial governor or city or municipal mayor, as the case may be. If the local chief executive concerned approves the same, he shall affix his signature on each 3 RESOLUTION NO. 0974-2023. TO SPELL our IN THE INDIGENOUS POLITICAL STRUCTURE (IPS) THE FOLLOWING: MUNICIPAL TRIBAL CHIEFTAIN. INDIGENOUS PEOPLE OFFICER, ANCESTRAL DOMAIN MANAGEMENT OFFICER. INDIGENOUS PEOPLE WOMEN. and every page thereof; otherwise, he shall veto it and return the same with his objections to the sanggunian, which may proceed to reconsider the same. The sanggunian concerned may override the veto of the local chief executive by two- thirds (2/3) vote of all its members, thereby making the ordinance or resolution effective for all legal intents and purposes. (b) The veto shall be communicated by the local chief executive concerned to the sanggunian within fifteen (15) days in the case of a province, and ten (10) days in the case of a city or a municipality; otherwise, the ordinance shall be deemed approved as if he had signed it. (c) Ordinances enacted by the sangguniang barangay shall, upon approval by the majority of all its members, be signed by the punong barangay." (Emphasis supplied) Parenthetically, Section 55 thereof provides: "Section 55. Veto Power of the Local Chief Executive. - (a) The local chief executive may veto any ordinance of the sanggunian panlalawigan, sangguniang panlungsod, or sanggunian bayan on the ground that it is ultra vires or prejudicial to the public welfare, stating his reasons therefor in writing (b) The local chief executive, except the punong barangay, shall have the power to veto any particular item or items of an appropriations ordinance, an ordinance or resolution adopting a local development plan and public investment program, or an ordinance directing the payment of money or creating liability. In such a case, the veto shall not affect the item or items which are not objected to. The vetoed item or items shall not take effect unless the sanggunian overrides the veto in the manner herein provided; otherwise, the item or items in the appropriations ordinance of the previous year corresponding to those vetoed, if any, shall be deemed reenacted. (c) The local chief executive may veto an ordinance or resolution only once. The sanggunian may override the veto of the local chief executive concerned by two- thirds (2/3) vote of all its members, thereby making the ordinance effective even without the approval of the local chief executive concerned." The foregoing provisions are the legal framework that primarily governs the dynamics of veto power granted to LCE. Notably, the language of the Code—insofar as the veto power of the LCE is concerned—is fundamentally focused on approved measures. Section 54 employs the term "enacted," referring to such an ordinance that shall be presented to the LCE for his consideration. Here, the term "enacted" suggests that a particular measure has already been approved at the sanggunian level. Accordingly, the veto power of the LCE is limited to measures that have been approved by the sanggunian, thereby implicitly excluding those that have been disapproved by the sanggunian. Elsewise stated, the exercise of veto power by the LCE does not extend to measures that have been disapproved by the sanggunian. It is important to note that when the sanggunian disapproves an ordinance or a resolution, it signifies that the majority of the sangguniang members do not favor or support the intent or the provisions of such a measure. Consequently, such disapproval renders the measure futile. Page 3 of 4

Pertinently, in DILG Legal Opinion No. 3, Series of 20235, we had the occasion to render an opinion on a relatively similar issue. In the said opinion, we opined that only measures that have been enacted—meaning, approved by the Sanggunian at its level—into an ordinance by the Sanggunian shall be submitted to the LCE for the latter to either approve or veto the same. Pertinent portion of which reads: "In the case at hand, the Sanggunian "disapproves" in its entirety the executive budget being proposed by the LCE. Such disapproval only means that no ordinance was ever enacted by the Sanggunian. Logically therefore, the LCE cannot yet exercise his/her approval or veto power since there is no enacted ordinance, so to speak, to be forwarded to him/her by the measure is considered a "lost measure" and, hence, there was nothing to be forwarded to the Governor for his/her approval or veto." Premised from the foregoing, this Department opines that LCEs are bereft of authority to veto a resolution that has been disapproved by the sanggunian. The Code does not clothe the LCE with the power to exercise his veto power over disapproved measures, thereby making the same "approved." Fundamentally, the veto power granted to LCEs does not operate to approve an ordinance or resolution that has been disapproved at the sanggunian level. Otherwise, it would undermine the legislative process, and ultimately, it would tantamount to encroachment of the functions of the sanggunian, which is antithetical to the system of check and balance between the legislative and executive departments of local governments. It is to be emphasized, however, that this Department is an agency under the executive branch of the government, and as such, it is devoid of authority to declare invalid or illegal any legislative measures enacted or passed by local government officials, nor does it have authority to declare invalid or illegal any acts committed by local government officials that are alleged to be in violation of the Local Government This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, y Authority of the cretary: AN VICTOR R.
